 Kings Trade Nique Clifford To Thunder For Two Second-Round Picks
 By Rory Maher |
 at November 8, 2026 2:47 pm 
 2:47 pm:  The trade is official, according to the Thunder, who announced in a press release that Terry was waived to make room for Clifford.
 12:18 pm: The Kings are trading Nique Clifford to the Thunder for two second-round picks, sources tell Shams Charania of ESPN ( Twitter links ).
 The second-rounders heading to the Kings will be Utah’s in 2028 and Minnesota’s in 2030, per Sam Amick of The Athletic ( Twitter link ). Both of the picks were controlled by the Thunder from previous trades.
 Charania hears Sacramento worked with Clifford to find a new home for the second-year wing, who was out of the team’s rotation this season. The former Colorado State guard was selected 24th overall in last year’s draft.
 The Thunder will have to clear a roster spot to add Clifford. The easiest player to waive would be Dalen Terry , who recently signed a non-guaranteed two-year deal with Oklahoma City, notes Rylan Stiles of SI.com ( via Twitter ).
 Clifford was technically drafted by the Thunder in 2025. The Kings acquired his rights by sending Oklahoma City the Spurs’ 2027 first-round pick — that selection is top-16 protected and will likely to convey to the Thunder next year.
 As ESPN’s Bobby Marks observes ( Twitter link ), that means the Thunder will essentially end up with Clifford and that Spurs pick for a pair of second-rounders, though obviously the two deals were made more than a year apart.
 Oklahoma City will use one of the three traded player exceptions it created this offseason to acquire Clifford, who earns $3.26MM this season and $3.42MM in 2027/28. The Thunder will have until November 1, 2027 to decide whether they want to exercise their $5.98MM option on Clifford for ’28/29.
 Since the Thunder generated the TPE they’ll use to take on Clifford during the 2026/27 league year, they won’t be hard-capped at the second tax apron, Marks tweets . OKC had up to 21 future second-round picks to include in a deal, Marks adds.
 The Thunder lost Jalen Williams , Cason Wallace and Chet Holmgren to long-term injuries (potentially season-ending for Williams and Wallace) in an Oct. 25 game vs. the Clippers. Despite the injuries, they’re currently 8-2 and are riding a four-game winning streak.
 The Kings, meanwhile, will create both a roster spot and some financial flexibility below the luxury tax line by sending out Clifford without receiving a player in return. Sacramento had zero future second-rounders prior to the deal, per Marks ( Twitter link ).
 Once the trade is official, the Kings will be at 13 players on standard contracts. They’ll have 14 days to fill one of their two 15-man roster openings, Marks notes.
 ESPN reported over a week ago that Clifford could be a trade target for the Thunder. At the time, the Kings were said to be reluctant to part with the 6’5″ guard/forward. According to Michael Scotto of HoopsHype ( Twitter link ), the Lakers and Nuggets both expressed interest in Clifford before the Kings agreed to trade him to the Thunder.
 Clifford raised his draft stock in 2024/25 after a strong “super senior” year with the Rams in which he averaged 18.9 points, 9.6 rebounds, 4.4 assists and 1.2 steals in 35.4 minutes per game across 36 starts, with a .496/.377/.777 shooting line. In 75 appearances (25.1 MPG) as a rookie last season, the 24-year-old averaged 8.6 PPG, 3.8 RPG, 2.4 APG and 0.9 SPG on .418/.333/.722 shooting splits.
 Despite being a rotation regular in 2025/26, Clifford has barely played this season for the 1-8 Kings, averaging just 6.3 MPG in eight appearances.
